 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3

 Keyonte George had himself a game with 39 points (14-of-26 FGs, 9-of-13 FTs), two rebounds, nine assists, four steals, a block, and two 3-pointers in overtime loss. 
 Keyonte had a bad couple of games but bounced back in a major way. The Jazz continue to run their offense around Keyonte George, and it’s been putting up fantasy numbers. He hasn’t put up the same number of numbers as last year, but he’s still leading the team in points and assists. He was one of the only players in this game that could shoot efficiently. It’s a nice development for where he started with his efficiency when he started his career.
 -  Brian Taylor

 Darryn Peterson 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #22 
 Personalize your Rotoworld feed by favoriting players 
 Darry Peterson recorded 16 points (6-of-15 FGs, 1-of-2 FTs), four rebounds, four assists, one steal, one block and three three-pointers in Saturday’s loss to the Trail Blazers. 
 Peterson has scored in double figures in each of Utah’s last three games. Against the Trail Blazers, he wasn’t at his best, committing three turnovers, but the rookie guard still finished with a full stat line. Peterson played the entire fourth quarter, sharing the court with Keyonte George (8/3/4/1) for seven minutes and Isaiah Collier (8/1/4/2) for the other five. According to Cleaning the Glass, Peterson has played 90% of his minutes at shooting guard thus far. That split appears unlikely to change anytime soon, which may lower his fantasy ceiling. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Keyonte George without Lauri or JJJ, put up 31 points (11-of-27 FGs, 4-of-4 FTs), four rebounds, three assists, five 3-pointers, and five turnovers in the 117-111 overtime loss to the Spurs. 
 Keyonte had a lot on his shoulders with the injuries to Jaren Jackson and Lauri Markkanen. He was the go to guy and helped keep the Jazz in the game. He was one of three people on the team to play more than thirty minutes in the loss. If you have Keyonte George in redraft leagues, it will be worth paying attention to how many points he’s scoring in case there is a sell-high window due the injuries and with Darryn continuing to get better. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Utah Jazz will start Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Josh Green, Ace Bailey, and Jaxson Hayes against the Spurs. 
 Josh Green will start in place of Lauri Markkanen tonight who is out with a wrist injury, and Jaxson Hayes will return to the starting lineup for the injured Jaren Jackson Jr. Green and Hayes can be used as streamers but neither will be factors in most redraft leagues. Look for Darryn and Ace to pick up the scoring in this game. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Keyonte George led the Jazz with 26 points (9-of-17 FGs, 8-of-9 FTs), three rebounds and six assists in a 110-105 loss to the Grizzlies on Monday. 
 It wasn’t enough to get the win, but George was the most productive scorer in this game. Both Lauri Markkanen (wrist) and Jaren Jackson Jr. (knee) exited early, which meant more offensive responsibility for George. If either, or both, misses time moving forward, George’s usage will continue to skyrocket. He has been excellent to start the year and will look to stay hot against the Spurs on Wednesday. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Keyonte George accounted for 24 points (7-of-13 FGs, 8-of-10 FTs), nine rebounds, 10 assists, one steal and two three-pointers in Sunday’s loss to the Lakers. 
 Lakers star Luka Dončić stole the show on Sunday, but George had a good day in his own right. The Jazz point guard finished one rebound shy of his first triple-double. George committed six turnovers, but the overall production helped compensate for that. He’s now dished out 10 assists in consecutive games, the first time George has done that since October 24-27, 2025. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Keyonte George had 19 points (6-of-12 FGs, 4-of-6 FTs), a rebound, ten assists, a steal, and three 3-pointers in wins against Pelicans. 
 Keyonte George was much better as a facilitator in this game which allowed players like Lauri to get better looks. He makes a lot of momentum gaining three pointers. Keyonte’s production has not dipped with the arrival of Darryn Peterson, and fantasy owners should be happy with that. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Keyonte George with 22 points (7-of-12 FGs, 4-of-7 FTs), three rebounds, five assists, and four 3-pointers in Wednesday’s season debut. 
 Keyonte George continued right where he left off last season and continued to get buckets. He will need to do more than score if he’s going to help lead the Jazz to the playoffs. He will likely continue to put up numbers throughout the year. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 Jazz will start Keyonte George, Darryn Peterson, Lauri Markkanen, Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jaxson Hayes against the Grizzlies on Wednesday. 
 George had a breakout season in 2025-26 and the Jazz rewarded him with a contract extension worth more than $150 million over five years. He’ll make his first start since signing his new deal alongside Peterson, Markkanen, Jackson and Hayes. 
 Keyonte George 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #3 
 ESPN’s Shams Charania reports that the Jazz and Keyonte George have agreed to a five-year, $157.5 million extension. 
 After two seasons of inconsistent play, George took a significant step forward in 2025-26. The 6-foot-4 point guard recorded career-high averages in points, assists and steals. Averaging 23.6 points, 3.7 rebounds, 6.1 assists, 1.1 steals and 2.5 three-pointers per game, George cemented his status as the point guard the Jazz will lean on as they look to move up the pecking order in the Western Conference. While having a healthy Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr. may cut into George’s scoring, his assist production could increase in 2026-27. 
 Isaiah Collier 
 UTA 
 Guard 
 #8 
 Isaiah Collier produced 21 points (9-of-21 FGs, 2-of-4 FTs), five rebounds, three assists, one steal, one block and one three-pointer in Sunday’s loss to the Kings. 
 Collier’s assist tally may not have been as robust as many fantasy managers hoped, with him starting for the injured Keyonte George. Still, he did record his second 20-point game in four appearances. Since the All-Star break, the second-year point guard has provided eighth-round value in eight-cat formats. With George not being re-evaluated until the final week of March, now is a good time to go all-in on Collier.

 Jamal Murray didn’t have the most efficient night but still filled up the stat sheet in the win. He really got going in the second half which helped the Nuggets take off in the third quarter.  Since moving into the Timberwolves’ starting lineup after Anthony Edwards underwent knee surgery, Dosunmu has scored at least 15 points in five straight games.  Nikola Jokić had himself a night with 32 points (13-of-19 FGs, 6-of-7 FTs), ten rebounds, eleven assists and three steals in 128-109 win over the Raptors.
 Jokić was a monster in this game and was a big reason why they won this game. We have seen some level of decline in terms of his on court play this season, but he’s still an elite fantasy player. He completely transformed this game in the second half where the Nuggets got off to a massive lead where he didn’t even play in the fourth quarter, so it could’ve been even better had it been a close game.

 Shai Gilgeous-Alexander had 42 points (11-of-26 FGs, 15-of-19 FTs), four rebounds, eight assists, one block and five three-pointers in the 124-116 victory over the Cavaliers on Wednesday. 
 Gilgeous-Alexander has destroyed the Cavaliers in the last two games. The two-time defending MVP has 85 points and two wins against Cleveland going all the way back to Monday. Gilgeous-Alexander can reach heights few players in the NBA can. He showed that again Wednesday and will likely continue to have some monster nights while the Thunder are missing multiple starters.

 LaMelo Ball tallied 20 points (6-of-11 FGs, 4-of-5 FTs), two rebounds, six assists, three steals, one block and four three-pointers in Wednesday’s win over the Rockets.
 After recording nearly as many turnovers (six) as points (eight) in the first three quarters of Wednesday’s game, Ball rose to the occasion in the fourth. Shooting 4-of-4 from the field and 2-of-3 from the foul line, the Timberwolves point guard scored 12 points in the fourth quarter. With Anthony Edwards (knee) out, the Timberwolves need Ball to be consistently efficient, and he’s been solid this week.

 Derik Queen got going in the fourth quarter and he helped get the Pelicans back in this game after the Jazz went on a big run.
